title: Private Helm: add batching_tier values + feature flag wiring for tiered defaults
author: Diego Santos
description:
Summary: This PR updates the redwood-private Helm chart to support selecting tiered batching defaults in Private deployments via values.yaml, and wires the selection into the runtime config map alongside a feature-flag style enablement switch. This is intended to mirror Hosted/Dedicated behavior (tier selection + safe rollout), while remaining backwards compatible with existing explicit batching knobs.

What’s included: (1) New values under runtime.config.batching with batchingTier: fast|standard|cost_efficient and enableTieredDefaults: true|false (default false for existing installs; can be enabled for new installs/early adopters). (2) Optional rollout controls under runtime.flags.tieredBatching (enabled + scope hints) that map to the runtime’s config flags (the runtime still owns actual percentage-based ramping; chart only passes through config). (3) values.schema.json validation and helpful descriptions to prevent invalid tier values. (4) README + upgrade notes describing precedence: explicit batching parameters (max_batch_size, max_queue_delay_ms, etc.) override batchingTier defaults; batchingTier only applies when explicit knobs are omitted.

Motivation: Private customers need a straightforward way to opt in to workload-aware batching defaults and to pass through the new tier selection without hand-editing ConfigMaps. This also supports CS/SE troubleshooting (INT-3301) by making the effective intent visible in a single values block.

Behavior / precedence: - If runtime.config.batching.enableTieredDefaults=false, chart emits no batching_tier field (status quo). - If enableTieredDefaults=true and batchingTier is set, chart emits batching_tier=<tier>. - If users set any explicit batching knobs (legacy fields), those are passed as-is and will override the tier defaults at runtime (per runtime precedence rules); docs call this out.

Upgrade notes (TL;DR): No action required. Existing Private installs will continue using explicit batching config or runtime defaults. To opt in: set runtime.config.batching.enableTieredDefaults=true and runtime.config.batching.batchingTier=standard (recommended for first beta cohort), apply via Helm upgrade, and monitor tier dashboards (latency p95/p99, queue delay, batch size distribution, timeout rate). If issues: set enableTieredDefaults=false and re-deploy (or pin explicit knobs).

Testing: - helm lint (chart + schema) - helm template rendered against minimal and full values - kubeconform validation for generated manifests - golden snapshot updated for ConfigMap payload changes

Follow-ups: - Once runtime-1.21 is the minimum supported version for Private, we can consider flipping enableTieredDefaults to true for new installs only (not upgrades) and adding a values migration helper in the installer repo.
commits: chart(redwood-private): add runtime.config.batching values + schema validation
templates: render batching_tier + enable flag into runtime ConfigMap
docs: add upgrade notes and examples for tier selection
chore: bump chart version + update changelog
conversation: Ethan Park (review): Can we ensure the tier value matches runtime enum exactly? I’ve seen cost-efficient vs cost_efficient drift.
Diego Santos (author): Good call. Updated schema + docs to use cost_efficient (matches runtime config). Also added a schema enum so invalid values fail at helm install time.
Rafael Mendes (review): Please add explicit upgrade guidance for existing customers and an easy rollback instruction. Also, I’d like enableTieredDefaults defaulting to false on upgrades.

Diego Santos (author): Added an Upgrade Notes section to README + changelog. Default remains false unless user sets it; rollback is just toggling enableTieredDefaults back to false and re-running helm upgrade.
Allison Grant (review): Any new metrics/labels being toggled here? We should avoid chart-side assumptions about SLO labels.
Diego Santos (author): No metrics changes in this chart. This only passes config fields through; observability pack handles dashboards/labels separately.
Alex Martinez (review): Can you add a short example snippet that shows choosing tier but overriding max_queue_delay_ms for streaming routes? (common question from DevEx/support)

Diego Santos (author): Added an example in README showing tier selection + explicit override note. The chart doesn’t do per-route config, but the example clarifies precedence and points to runtime config docs.
Ethan Park (approval): LGTM after schema enum + doc tweaks.
Rafael Mendes (approval): Approved. Please ensure release notes mention default is off for upgrades.
release_notes: Private Helm chart now supports tiered batching defaults configuration. New values: runtime.config.batching.enableTieredDefaults (default false) and runtime.config.batching.batchingTier (fast|standard|cost_efficient). Explicit batching knobs still override tier defaults. Includes upgrade/rollback guidance in README + changelog.
